newsitem.title: UK: UK gives Channel 5 UHF channel access for 5 years.
newsitem.headline: UK gives Channel 5 UHF channel access for 5 years.

text.p: The UK's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said on Monday that Channel 5, the first new terrestrial channel to be launched for 14 years, would have access to UHF channel 35 for five years.
This will enhance Channel 5's initial audience, the DTI said in a statement.
The arrangements agreed with Channel 5 Broadcasting (C5B) "will ensure that both the UK's future digital TV needs can be met and that C5B can maximise its launch audience".

Channel 35 will be returned for new broadcast services "as the market for advanced digital television develops and C5B viewers on Channel 35 will be moved to alternative means of service delivery at that time, the DTI added.
The agreement was welcomed by the Secretary of State for National Heritage Virginia Bottomley.
"This agreement will bring the new channel to at least three million viewers who would not otherwise have been able to see it," Bottomley said in a statement.
